accepted every value and could not throw, before the repair or after it; what it did was
truncate.  `probes/r2d` records what that cost: `n: NN32 = 4294967296`, a numeral one above
the largest `NN32`, was silently `0`, and now raises `Not in range for NN32: 4294967296`.
The same vacuity accepted the `BOGUS` sentinel `0xdeadbeefcafebabe` that a string-carried
literal leaves in `smallerVal` (`:25,37`).

## What part one uncovered, and the second half of the rung

`library_tests/Integer.test` is the corpus file the change reaches.  Before the repair it
was green, 27 tests (`probes/integer-test-before.out`).  After part one it had four
failures (`probes/integer-test-after.out`), and all four are one thing:

| test | thrown | site |
|---|---|---|
| `AverageTest` | `Not in range for ZZ32: 2147483648` | the **prelude**, `fortress.CompilerLibrary$ZZ32_MIN.<clinit>`, `Library/CompilerLibrary.fss:569` |
| `Integer3` | `Not in range for ZZ32: 2684354560` | `library_tests/Integer3.fss:46` |
| `Integer4` | `Not in range for ZZ64: 11529215046068469760` | `library_tests/Integer4.fss:46` |
| `IntegerChoose2` | `Not in range for ZZ32: 3037000500` | `library_tests/IntegerChoose2.fss:114` |

The first three are one idiom: a radix-16 numeral whose value is outside the annotated
signed type, written to mean the two's-complement bit pattern.  `ZZ32_MIN: ZZ32 =
8000'0000_16` means the `ZZ32` whose pattern is `0x80000000`; `twiceHuge: ZZ32 =
A0000000_16` means the `ZZ32` whose pattern is `0xA0000000`.  `literals.tex:104-108` gives
those numerals the values $2^{31}$ and $2684354560$, and the language has no bit-pattern
reading of a numeral.

`probes/r2g` and `probes/r2h` settle it: the interpreter has always refused the idiom —
`a: ZZ32 = 8000'0000_16` is "RHS expression type Long is not assignable to LHS type ZZ32",
and `a: ZZ64 = 8000'0000'0000'0000_16` is the same for `BigNum`.  So these are not correct
programs the repair broke.  They are programs the language does not accept, which the
compile path accepted only because the wrap turned them into something else, and on which
the two paths now **agree**.  The repair reduces the divergence between `walk` and the
compiled run on every case this section measures.  It does create one, which this report
first denied and the skeptic measured: `compiler-probes/p37.fss` compares a numeral of bit
length 64, and once that numeral correctly keeps its decimal string the comparison raises
`Not in range for ZZ64: 18446744073709551615`, because `trait IntLiteral`'s comparisons are
performed at `ZZ64` (`LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:837-842`, rung 6's repair) and
`FIntLiteral.asZZ64` throws for a string-carried numeral (`FIntLiteral.java:74-77`).  `walk`
prints three `false` lines, which `literals.tex:83-86` requires; before the repair the
compiled run printed `true`, silently wrong.  Loud and wrong-in-shape is better than quiet
and wrong in value, so the repair stands and ledger row 328 is opened for the comparison
site; the probes are `probes/skeptic/p37.walk.skeptic` and `p37.compiled.skeptic`, and
`p37a`, whose numerals are inside `ZZ64`, agrees on both paths.

The complete blast radius was measured rather than guessed: every numeral in the corpora
and the libraries whose value has bit length exactly 32 or exactly 64 was enumerated by
value, in every radix (`probes/boundary-numerals.txt`).  Eighteen of those lines are on the
compile path.  Twelve are in range for their annotated type (`CompilerLibrary.fss:574,576`
`NN32_MAX` and `NN64_MAX`, `ShiftTest.fss:32,33`, `NN32.fss:43,46`, `NN64.fss:45,46,48`,
`ZZ.fss:44`, `AverageTest.fss:118`, `ShiftTest2.fss:194`) and are now correct where they had
been right only by the wrap's accident.  Six are out of range: the five repaired here
(`CompilerLibrary.fss:569,571`, `Integer3.fss:46`, `Integer4.fss:46`,
`IntegerChoose2.fss:114`) and `library_tests/ChooseTest3.fss:125`, which is in no `.test`
file (`LibraryJUTest.java:36` sweeps `.test` files only), so it is not gated and is left for
the record rather than edited unverified.  The remaining lines the enumeration shows are in
the interpreter-only libraries `Library/QuickCheck.fss` and `Library/Random.fss`, which are
not part of the compile-path prelude, in `ProjectFortress/tests/`, whose two hits are
untyped comparisons of the same numeral to itself (`NumeralTest.fss:44-45`) and numerals
inside string literals, and in this rung's own test.

### The four repairs, and why each is the smallest faithful one

`Library/CompilerLibrary.fss:569,571` — `ZZ32_MIN` and `ZZ64_MIN` rewritten as
`-7FFF'FFFF_16 - 1` and `-7FFF'FFFF'FFFF'FFFF_16 - 1`, the spelling of
`FortressLibrary.fss:703`.  `ZZ32_MAX`, `NN32_MIN`, `NN32_MAX`, `NN64_MIN` and `NN64_MAX`
beside them are all in range and untouched.  `probes/r2i` confirms both values on both
paths: `-2147483648` and `-9223372036854775808`, identical in `walk` and compiled.

`library_tests/Integer3.fss:46` — `twiceHuge: ZZ32 = A0000000_16` becomes `-60000000_16`,
and `Integer4.fss:46` — `A000000000000000_16` becomes `-6000000000000000_16`.  These are
**value-preserving**: `0xA0000000` read as a signed 32-bit value is `-0x60000000 =
-1610612736`, and `0xA000000000000000` as signed 64-bit is `-0x6000000000000000 =
-6917529027641081856` (`probes/r2i`, third and fourth lines).  The assertions these feed —
`(huge BOXPLUS huge) = twiceHuge` at `Integer3.fss:99`, `(huge BOXMINUS minusHuge) =
twiceHuge` at `:106`, and the two in `Integer4` at `:99,106` — continue to assert exactly
what they asserted: that wrapping addition of `0x50000000 + 0x50000000` yields the `ZZ32`
whose pattern is `0xA0000000`.  Nothing is weakened and no assertion is removed.

`library_tests/IntegerChoose2.fss` — `3037000500` is bound at `ZZ64` before the loop
(`fastSlowBoundary: ZZ64 = 3037000500`, added among the file's own twenty-one `ZZ64`
constant bindings at `:35-55`) and the call at `:115` reads that binding.  The numeral was
being coerced at `ZZ32` because the loop variable `j` is a `ZZ32`, and `3037000500` is
outside `ZZ32`.  This one is not only an illegal program: under the wrap the test was
exercising `i = -1257966796`, not the $\sqrt{2^{63}}$ boundary its own comment at `:111-112`
names, so the assertion it makes was never the assertion it claims.  Binding the constant
at `ZZ64` is the file's own established idiom — it is why `zero: ZZ64 = 0` through
`eightyone: ZZ64 = 81` exist — and it makes the test exercise what it says.

## The stop condition, tested and not met

`REPAIR-BATCH.md` §R2 and the brief name one stop: if the repair forces a choice of which
number type an untyped literal's arithmetic happens at, that is Pavol's call.

**It does not force that choice, and the reason is structural.**  All three branches of
`forIntLiteralExpr` call `FIntLiteral.make` and all three produce an `FIntLiteral`; the
branch selects an overload (`int`, `long`, `String`), never a type.  The static type of the
expression is `Types.INT_LITERAL` in every case (`Misc.scala:467-468`).  So the repair
changes what value the literal carries and nothing about where its arithmetic happens.

Measured, not only argued: `probes/r2e` and rung 7's `p39` run the two mechanisms side by
side.  Before the repair, `println (4294967295 + 1)` folded to `4294967296` while `a =
4294967295; b = 1; println (a + b)` gave `0`.  After it, both give `4294967296`, which is
what `walk` gives.  The arithmetic still happens at `IntLiteral`, through rung 7's helpers,
exactly as before; it now starts from the right operand.

The fork `REPAIR-BATCH.md` describes — which number type an untyped numeral's arithmetic
happens at, where the compiler folds exactly before typecheck and the interpreter computes
at the narrowest applicable type — is untouched and still open.

## Decisions taken inside the rung

**Repairing the prelude and three corpus files rather than stopping.**  The alternative was
to report part one's four red tests to Pavol and land nothing.  It was rejected because
`PLAN.md:47` is explicit that "any source in the tree may be edited under the rule above;
which file it is in is not a decision", because none of that clause's stops fires here (no
design fork; the change of semantics is *toward* the specification, not against it; no test
is deleted; this is the first repair, not a gate red twice), and because the prelude half is
forced in any case: with `CompilerLibrary.fss:569` as written, `ZZ32_MIN`'s class
initialiser throws and nothing on the compile path that touches the number properties runs
at all.  The decision is recorded here because it widens the rung past the two files the
brief named.

**Value-preserving rewrites in the corpus, not moves to `not_working_library_tests/`.**
Moving `Integer3` and `Integer4` was the alternative.  It was rejected because a faithful
rewrite exists and is exact, and because those two files are the only tests of the
`BOXPLUS`/`BOXMINUS`/`BOXDOT`/`DOTPLUS` wrapping and saturating operators at `ZZ32` and
`ZZ64` (`Integer3.fss:97-126`), which is coverage the corpus would not get back.

**`asNN32` repaired although nothing forced it.**  The alternative was to leave a vacuous
range check in place beside a repaired `asNN64`.  It was rejected because the check is
three lines from the comment that asks for this rung — "This is a cheap fix. Problem in
codeGen.forIntLiteral" (`FIntLiteral.java:79` before the repair) — and because leaving it
would keep a silent truncation (`probes/r2d`) in the one getter the rung was already
rewriting.  The report says plainly that this is a decision and that the brief's premise
about it, that `asNN32` "currently depends on the wrap" and would "begin throwing", is true
of `asNN64` and not of `asNN32`.

**Three branches kept, not collapsed to `simpleIntLiteralArith`'s two.**
`FIntLiteral.make(int)` and `make(long)` both store a `long`, so the int branch buys nothing
at run time and the two-branch form would have been a smaller edit.  It is kept because the
bytecode optimizer matches on it: `RemoveLiteralCoercions.removeIntLiterals`
(`compiler/asmbytecodeoptimizer/RemoveLiteralCoercions.java:33-53`) replaces
`FIntLiteral.make(I)` followed by `coerce_ZZ32` with `FZZ32.make(I)`, and collapsing the int
branch would switch that substitution off for every small literal.  The repair also makes
that substitution sound: it elides `asZZ32`'s range check, which is safe exactly when the
int branch is the `ZZ32`-representable range — true under `l <= 31`, false under `l <= 32`.
This argument is about dormant code and is not claimed as live behaviour: the optimizer is
reached only from `ByteCodeOptimizer.main` (`ByteCodeOptimizer.java:130,146`), nothing in
`Shell` or the compiler driver calls it, and its 226 tests are switched off at
`default_repository/configuration:50-51` (`map/dormant-code.md:188`).

**`asZZ32` left alone.**  For a string-carried numeral it is correct only by accident:
`smallerVal` holds `BOGUS`, which falls outside `int` range, so the check refuses it.
Adding `largerVal == null` would change no behaviour today and was left out to keep the
diff to what the tests need; the dependency on the sentinel's value is recorded here.

**The test's expected values are computed, not written twice.**  Every expectation in
`compiler_tests/IntLiteralWrapRepairR2.fss` is built at run time from numerals of bit length
16, 17, 31, 33 and 63, none of which any branch of the split ever mis-read, following
`library_tests/IntLiteralArithRung7.fss:39-43`.  A literal `4294967295` on the expected side
would have wrapped identically and the test would have passed before the repair.

**The test is in `compiler_tests/`, not `library_tests/`.**  `PLAN.md` step 1 of the order of
work puts codegen rungs there, and `CompilerJUTest.java:36,42` sweeps that directory in
`testFast` (`build.xml:965`).

## The failure-mode question

**One loud failure becomes a quiet value, and this report first did not say so.**
`FIntLiteral.asNN64`'s pre-image was `if (largerVal == null) return
FNN64.make((long)smallerVal); throw outOfRange("NN64");` -- it threw for *every*
string-carried numeral -- and `simpleIntLiteralArith.fromBigInteger` sends every `IntLiteral`
arithmetic result of bit length 64 or more to the string branch (`:31-32`), a path this rung
does not touch.  So the transition is reachable without a numeral of bit length 64 anywhere
in the source.  The skeptic's probe `probes/skeptic/s3.fss` is the case: `x =
9223372036854775807` then `n: NN64 = x + x + 1` raised `Error: Not in range for NN64:
18446744073709551615` before this rung and now computes the value, which
`probes/skeptic/s3.compiled` shows **rendered as `-1`**.

The value is the specification-correct one -- `literals.tex:83-86` gives the numeral its
exact value and $2^{64}-1$ is inside `NN64` -- so the quiet answer is right where the loud
failure was wrong.  The cost is nonetheless real and is the reason this belongs with the
rendering row rather than beside it: the error that *named* the true value is gone, and what
replaces it prints as `-1`, because `FNN64.toString` is signed (`runtimeValues/FNN64.java:20`).
That is ledger row 326, and the two facts are one situation.  `walk` has no counterpart: it
refuses the coercion outright (`probes/skeptic/s3.walk`, "RHS expression type Long is not
assignable to LHS type NN64").

In the other direction -- a quiet wrong value becoming a loud failure -- there are four:
`asZZ32`, `asZZ64` and `asNN32` now raise `Not in range for ...` where they silently
truncated, which row 325 records for annotated declarations; `asNN32` on a string-carried
numeral now raises where it returned the `BOGUS` sentinel's low half
(`probes/skeptic/s2`); and `p37`'s comparison, row 328.

## Divergences between `walk` and the compiled run

| probe | before | after | what the specification says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `r2a` boundary numerals at `ZZ`, `ZZ64` | walk `4294967295` / `18446744073709551615`; compiled `-1` / `-1` | identical both ways | `literals.tex:83-86`: against the compiled run; repaired |
| `r2e`, `p39` literal arithmetic through bindings | walk `4294967296`; compiled `0` | identical both ways | `literals.tex:83-86` with `basic-integers.tex:368-370`: against the compiled run; repaired |
| `r2g`, `r2h` bit-pattern numeral at a signed type | walk refuses; compiled silently `-1` | both refuse | `literals.tex:104-108`: against the compiled run; repaired, and the four sites that relied on it repaired with it |
| `r2b` `NN32`/`NN64` rendering | walk refuses the coercion; compiled prints `-1` for both | unchanged | not settled by this rung's reading; a ledger row is owed, see below |
| `r2c`, `r2d`, `r2f` out-of-range coercions | walk refuses; compiled silently truncates | walk refuses; compiled raises `Not in range for ...` | the paths now agree in outcome and differ only in whether the diagnostic is static or dynamic; recorded, not repaired |
| `p37` comparison of a numeral of bit length 64 | walk three `false` lines; compiled `true` | walk unchanged; compiled raises `Not in range for ZZ64: 18446744073709551615` | `literals.tex:83-86`: against the compiled run both before and after -- a quiet wrong answer became a loud one, and the comparison site is ledger row 328, outside this rung |

`r2b` is the one divergence this rung leaves unchanged; `p37` and the `r2c`/`r2d`/`r2f`
class it changes without closing, as the table above records.  The compiled `NN32` and
`NN64` hold the right value — `IntLiteralWrapRepairR2.fss:64,69` assert `n32 = h32u + h32u + one32u` and `n64 =
h64u + h64u + one64u` and both pass — but render it signed, because `FNN32.toString` and
`FNN64.toString` are `String.valueOf(val)` over a signed `int` and `long`
(`runtimeValues/FNN32.java:19-20`, `FNN64.java:20`).  That is a rendering defect in the
unsigned runtime values, independent of this rung, and the record below opens it.

## The ladder subset: there is none, and why

`explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv` records, for every file of the ladder corpus, the
`fortress compile` return code and then the `fortress run` return code
(`run-ladder.sh:106-108`).  Every file of that corpus holding a numeral of bit length 32 or
64 — `NumeralTest.fss`, `NumberPrintTest.fss`, `formatTest.fss`, `sequivTest.fss`,
`BitTwiddle.fss`, `UnsignedTest.fss`, `BigNum.fss`, `simpleExp.fss`, `realArith.fss` — has
compile return code `255` and an empty run column: each fails in one or two seconds, before
code generation.  So no ladder row can move either way, and the driver was not run, which
also avoids its shared default root (`run-ladder.sh:22`) and its `experiment/env.sh` sweep
of `/tmp/fortress*rats` while the other rung is live.

## Recorded failure and recorded pass

Failure, before any edit existed: `probes/junit-before.out` — `. run
compiler_tests/IntLiteralWrapRepairR2 (271ms) FAIL: ZZ from the 32-bit numeral: -1 should be
4294967295`, `Tests run: 2, Failures: 1`.

The intermediate state, part one only: `probes/junit-codegen-only.out` — `Not in range for
NN64: 18446744073709551615` from `FIntLiteral.asNN64`, which is the coupling the brief
predicted, measured.

Pass: `probes/junit-after.out` (part one), `probes/junit-repaired.out` (after the four
further repairs) and `probes/junit-final.out` (the tree as it is left) — `. run
compiler_tests/IntLiteralWrapRepairR2 (430ms) PASS`, `OK (2 tests)`.

The corpus differential: `probes/integer-test-before.out` (`OK (27 tests)`),
`probes/integer-test-after.out` (part one only: four failures), `probes/integer-test-repaired.out`
(after the four repairs).

## Not done

`library_tests/ChooseTest3.fss:125` carries the same out-of-range numeral as
`IntegerChoose2.fss:114` and is in no `.test` file, so no gate covers it and no measurement
of a repair to it would be available here.  It is named in `record.md` for the ledger.

The static diagnostic.  `literals.tex:83-86` gives a numeral a type carrying its value, so
`a: ZZ32 = 4294967295` should be a static error; on this path it is a run-time one, because
the checker gives every numeral the same flat `Types.INT_LITERAL`
(`Misc.scala:467-468`) and `CompilerBuiltin.fsi:370-376` has no static parameter on
`IntLiteral`.  Recorded in `record.md`, not repaired: it is a checker and prelude rung.

`FNN32.toString` and `FNN64.toString` render an unsigned value signed.  Recorded in
`record.md`, not repaired.

**Rule 3 in passing.** Rows 314 and 316 of the gap ledger, and the comment at `ProjectFortress/library_tests/IntLiteralArithRung7.fss:30-31`, cite `Specification/library/apis/FortressLibrary.tex`, `…/CompilerLibrary.tex` and `…/CompilerBuiltin.tex`. So an `(api listing)` citation under `Specification/library/apis/` is not merely circular in the sense of `Specification/library/structure.tex:25-31`; it cites a path that is not in the tree and cannot be opened. This rung cites no such path.

## 4. The four deviations, each a decision

**(i) `floor` and `ceiling` return `RR64`, where the specification says ℤ.** Alternatives: `RR64`, which is precedent (d) — the team's commented-out draft in this very file — and also precedent (a), the interpreter's method type; or `ZZ64`, which is the specification's ℤ and the interpreter's *bracket* type. `RR64` was chosen. The reason is not that the specification is silent; it is that the specification requires the method and its enclosing operator to be the same operation with the same result (`numbers.tex:464`, `:467`, "likewise the enclosing operator"), the compiler prelude's two brackets are already declared `RR64` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:437-438`), and changing a declared type the prelude already has is one of the two stops CLIMB-BATCH-1.md reserves. Declaring the methods `ZZ64` would have satisfied the specification's magnitude and broken its identity, leaving one trait in which `floor(x)` and `⌊x⌋` have different types. Declaring them `RR64` keeps the trait coherent and leaves a single pre-existing deviation, now written down as a ledger row rather than doubled.

**(ii) `round` and `truncate` return `ZZ64`.** No enclosing operator for either exists in the compiler prelude, so (i)'s constraint does not apply; `ZZ64` is both the precedent (`FortressBuiltin.fss:187-190`) and an integer type, which is what ℤ asks for. The alternative, `RR64` for symmetry with `floor` and `ceiling`, was rejected: it would deviate from the specification and from the precedent at once, for symmetry alone.

**(iii) `round` is built on `Math.rint`, not `Math.round`.** `Math.round` rounds an exact half toward positive infinity; `Math.rint` rounds it to the even integer, which is the rule `numbers.tex:470-472` states. **That clause's reach, stated rather than assumed**: `Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex` has one section, "Rational Numbers" (`:16`), so the rule is stated of ℚ; ℚ is a subtype of ℝ in the prose (`:37`) and of `RR64` in the library (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:370`), so it runs from the supertype's direction and does not reach `RR64` by inheritance, and no prose chapter covers the real types. What carries the rule here is therefore the implementation's own ℚ body rather than the clause alone — plus IEEE 754, whose default rounding mode is round-half-to-even, which is what `Math.rint` implements. The interpreter's `Float$Round` is `Math.round(x)` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/Float.java:382-385`), so this is a deliberate deviation from precedent (b) — taken because precedent (c), the team's own ℚ body at `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:589`, implements the specification's rule in Fortress, and because a gated interpreter test asserts it: `ProjectFortress/tests/RationalTest.fss:428` asserts `round(15/6) = 2`, that is `round(2.5) = 2`. The differential in section 6 shows `walk` answering `3` for the same value at `RR64`. Ledger row (provisional 329) carries the interpreter-side defect.

**(iv) `atan2` takes `x: RR64` where the interpreter takes `x: Number`.** The compiler world's `Number` is an empty marker (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:96`, `spec-to-implementation.md:410`) and carries no arithmetic, and every binary declaration in the compiler world's `trait RR64` narrows the interpreter's `Number` parameter to `RR64` already (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:419-435` against `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:291-316`). So the type follows the file. The parameter **name** `x` is kept from the interpreter rather than renamed to the file's usual `other`, because for `atan2` the name carries meaning: `self` is the *y* coordinate and the argument is the *x* coordinate, which is what `Float.java:334-337` computes (`ATan2 extends RR2R`, `f(y, x) = Math.atan2(y, x)`, with `RR2R.applyMethod(FObject x, FValue y)` at `:86-92` putting `self` first).

**A fifth decision, about the natives' home.** The eleven new static methods went into `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleDoubleArith.java`, the team's own file, rather than into a new file beside it as rung 7 did with `simpleIntLiteralArith.java`. The criterion is the one that made rung 7 split: its helper dealt in a Fortress type and needed a clause in `NamingCzar.fortressTypeForForeignJavaType` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java:343-344`). These eleven deal in `double` and `long`, which the generic path maps without a clause (`NamingCzar.java:441-446`, `s(Type.LONG_TYPE, fortLib, "ZZ64")` and `s(Type.DOUBLE_TYPE, fortLib, "RR64")`), and they are the same kind of one-line wrapper over `java.lang.Math` as the file's existing `doublePow`, `doubleSQRT`, `doubleFloor`, `doubleCeiling` and `doubleAbs`. A new file would have split the double primitives across two files with no criterion. Worth noting for the next rung that touches this: `doubleTruncate` and `doubleRound` are the first natives in the tree that take a `double` and return a `long`.

**A sixth decision, about the test's assertions.** The comparing `assert` has no `RR64` form — rung 4 added `ZZ32`, `String` and `Character` only (`Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:45-49`) — and this rung did not add one. The alternative, adding `assert(x: RR64, y: RR64)` and `assert(x: RR64, y: RR64, failMsg: String)` to `CompilerLibrary`, was rejected for two reasons: rung T of this batch is editing `CompilerLibrary` in the same wave, and batch rule 1 keeps the merge clean by keeping the rungs' declarations disjoint; and floating-point assertions want an epsilon rather than `=`, which a comparing `assert` cannot express. The test therefore uses the Boolean form over `opr =` for the exact cases and over a local `near` for the inexact ones, and `.asZZ32` into rung 4's `ZZ32` form for `round` and `truncate` — the same idiom as `ProjectFortress/library_tests/IntLiteralArithRung7.fss:58-70`.

## 5. The edit

Four files, 82 added lines and 3 removed.

`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleDoubleArith.java:92-134`: eleven static methods, one line of body each — `doubleSin`, `doubleCos`, `doubleTan`, `doubleASin`, `doubleACos`, `doubleATan`, `doubleATan2`, `doubleLog`, `doubleExp` over `java.lang.Math`; `doubleTruncate(double a) { return (long) a; }`, the C cast the interpreter's `Float$Truncate` also uses (`Float.java:376-379`); and `doubleRound(double a) { return (long) Math.rint(a); }`. The capitalisation `ASin`/`ACos`/`ATan`/`ATan2` follows the interpreter's glue class names (`Float.java:316-338`); nothing in the file needed changing.

## 1. Where this belongs, and why here

The map's row for the numeric tower sends every prelude question to §4.2-4.3 of `explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md` (`spec-to-implementation.md:323`), whose table of the compiler prelude says `RR64` is "present, **flat**: … with `+`, `-`, `/`, `juxtaposition`, `DOT`, `^`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `SQRT` and the comparisons all declared on the trait itself (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:412-441`)" (`spec-to-implementation.md:411`).

So the declaration site is `trait RR64` in `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi` and its body in `.fss`, and the same map says operator and functional-method declarations inside a compiler-prelude trait are the established shape, not an invention: "**yes** — the compiler prelude declares its own operators this way (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:412-441`)" (`spec-to-implementation.md:356`).

The native side is equally settled: the compiler world's one Java-interop mechanism is `import java` over `nativeHelpers/`, read by `ForeignJava` with ASM and wrapped by `FortressTransformer` into `nativewrapper_cache` (`explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:441-449`, and the divergence table at `:483`, "Natives | `builtinPrimitive` + `interpreter/glue/` | `import java` + `nativeHelpers/` + `nativeInterface/`"); `spec-to-implementation.md:157` records the same for the feature row "foreign import".

Nothing about this rung touches a phase: the names are missing from the prelude, so every blocked file dies in disambiguation with `Variable <name> is not defined` (`explorations/compile-ladder/after/raw/tests/buffons.fss.compile` and six more), which is a library gap and not a checker or codegen gap. **(a) The interpreter's api, on `trait Number`.** `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:319-332` declares `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `asin`, `acos`, `atan`, `atan2(self, x: Number)`, `log`, `exp`, `floor` and `ceiling` returning `RR64`, the two enclosing operators `opr |\self/|` and `opr |/self\|` returning `ZZ64`, and `truncate` returning `ZZ64`. `round` is **not** in this api at all.

The glue is `java.lang.Math`, one method each, in `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/Float.java:298-386`.

**And those two bodies do not agree with the api or with each other on the return type of the two truncating methods.** `trait Number`'s own body, in the same trait the api at (a) describes (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:349-420`), declares `truncate(self):RR64` at `:418` and `round(self): ZZ` at `:419`, where the api declares `truncate(self):ZZ64` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:332`) and `object Float`'s body declares both `ZZ64` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:188-191`). Nothing rejects the disagreement because the static type checker does not run on the walk path, which is rule 4 of the prefix in miniature. It is recorded here because it is the strongest evidence that the return types of these four methods were never settled in the interpreter world either, and that is the substance of ledger row 330 rather than a defect this rung introduces.

**(c) The interpreter's `trait QQ`, which follows the specification where (a) and (b) do not.** `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:396-401` declares `floor`, `ceiling`, `truncate` and `round` on ℚ returning `ZZ` — the specification's ℤ — and `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:589` gives `round` a hand-written round-half-to-even body. **(d) The team's own draft for the compiler world**, commented out in the file being edited: `ceiling(self):RR64` and `floor(self):RR64` at `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:439-440`, with both natives already bound (`simpleDoubleArith.doubleFloor => jDoubleFloor`, `doubleCeiling => jDoubleCeiling`, `CompilerBuiltin.fss:212-213`) and already used by the enclosing operators of the same trait at `.fss:898-899`. Those two enclosing operators return `RR64` in the compiler world (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:437-438`), where the interpreter's return `ZZ64`.

The in-file shape copied for the body is `opr SQRT(self): RR64 = jDoubleSQRT(self)` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:900`, pre-edit), with its native bound in the `import java` block at `.fss:196-214`.

No corpus file competes for any of the thirteen names. `grep -rnE "(sin|cos|tan|asin|acos|atan|atan2|log|exp|floor|ceiling|truncate|round)[[:space:]]*\([[:space:]]*self"` over `ProjectFortress/tests` and every `*_tests/` directory returns nothing, and a declaration-shaped grep over the same eight directories returns only uses. The one place the names are declared again is the target program itself, at the array level and deliberately overloaded with the scalar: `exp[\T extends Number, I\](a: Array[\T,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](exp)` (`explorations/apl/mg/FlatArrays2.fss:44-45`), which is why the scalar must be a functional method nameable as a bare `exp`.

## 3. The specification, read

`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex` is chapter 33, "Numbers", and it has exactly one section, "Rational Numbers" (`:12-17`); the ℝ types appear in it only as names inside the subtype lists of the ℚ family (`:37-90`). The four rounding methods are declared at `:457-462` and defined in prose at `:464-477`: `floor` "returns the largest integer that is not greater", `ceiling` "the smallest integer that is not less", `round` "returns the integer that is closest … but if this rational number is exactly halfway between two consecutive integers, then `round` returns whichever of the two integers is **even**", `truncate` "returns the ceiling … if it is negative, and otherwise … the floor", that is toward zero. `:464` and `:467` both say "likewise the enclosing operator", so the specification makes the named method and the bracket the same operation with the same result type.

**A correction to the brief.** CLIMB-BATCH-1.md section F says "the 'Real' numbers section of that chapter is commented out (`numbers.tex:920`)". There is no such section and no such line: the file is 566 lines long and has no second section, commented out or otherwise, and no file under `Specification/basic-lib` or `Specification/advanced-lib` reaches line 920 except `advanced-lib/binary.tex`. The chapter's many `%` lines are the ASCII sources of the typeset displays, as `explorations/coordinator/map/design-intent-sources.md:104` already records for `algebraic-constraints.tex`; they are not disabled text. The conclusion the brief drew from the wrong citation is nevertheless right — the specification has no chapter for the real types — but it is right because the chapter was never written, not because it was switched off.

For `exp`, `log` and the trigonometric functions the prose is silent in the sense that matters (no definition and no declaration), but it is not silent about their existence, and two passages are worth having on the record because they are the closest the prose comes: `Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex:123-133` lists "`+`, `-`, `×`, `·`, `/`, `!`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `√`, `floor`, `ceiling`, `hyperfloor`, `hyperceiling`, `gcd`, `lcm`, `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `arcsin`, `arccos`, `arctan`" as the operations that may combine numeric **static** expressions — naming six of the transcendentals in mathematical spelling (`arcsin`, not `asin`), defining none, and not naming `exp`, `log` or `atan2` at all; and `Specification/basic/dimensions.tex:214-215` presumes them as library functions — "Other numerical functions, such as `sin` and `log`, require dimensionless arguments."

Neither passage constrains a return type or an argument type, so for the nine non-rounding methods the precedent of section 2 governs, as the brief says.

## 5. The decision

**The specification's spelling of the empty case was taken, not the corpus's**: `Maybe[\T\] comprises { Just[\T\], NothingObject[\T\] }` with `coerce(_: Nothing) = NothingObject[\T\]` and a separate `value object Nothing end`. This was a decision, and the code did not force it.

**The two candidates cannot coexist, measured.** `probes/DualNothing.fss` declares both spellings of one name in one scope under local names — `value object NothingD[\T extends Any\] extends MaybeD[\T\]` and then `value object NothingD end`. `probes/DualNothing.txt`: the non-parametric declaration takes the name, and both the parametric declaration's own header (`:16`) and the `comprises` clause that mentions it (`:8`) become errors — "Incorrect number of static arguments for type 'NothingD': provided 1, expected 0". So the fork is binary and there is no overload that serves both spellings.

**Why the specification cannot simply be transcribed.** `probes/WhereClauseNothing.fss` is `convenience.tex:49` under local names — `object NothingW extends MaybeW[\T\] where {T extends Object}`. `probes/WhereClauseNothing.txt` records the same single error from `fortress compile` and from `fortress walk`, both rc=255: `T is undefined`, at the `T` inside the extends clause. Name resolution does not let a where clause bind a type variable used in an extends clause, on either path, so neither implementation can express the declaration the specification writes; `CodeGen.java:4088` (`forObjectDeclPrePass`, `header.getWhereClause().isNone()`) would refuse it at codegen even if name resolution admitted it. The compensating mechanism is coercion, which the compile path has and the interpreter does not (`explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:288`: "nothing: no occurrence of `Coercion` or `coerce` anywhere under `interpreter/`"). That is why the team's draft for this world spells the empty case as it does and the interpreter's prelude does not: the interpreter had no way to write it, and said so at `FortressLibrary.fss:1340-1341`.

**What decided it.** Three things point one way. The prose says `Nothing` is one object (`convenience.tex:49`) and uses it as a value at a `Maybe[\String\]` (`exceptions.tex:122`). The team, writing for *this* world, chose that shape (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229`) and used it in all seven of its own draft tests. And the interpreter's own author records that the parametric form is a workaround for a missing feature, not the design. The compiler world has the compensating feature, and `probes/MaybeCoercionSites.txt` records it working in all three positions the specification writes an unparameterised `Nothing` in — a declared-type binding, a getter's default, a function argument — with `typecase` confirming the coerced value is a `NothingObject[\ZZ32\]` at run time. Against that stands corpus usage, which is evidence of what was written, not of what the language is (rule 4).

**The alternative and its cost.** Taking the corpus's `Nothing[\T\]` would remove the one error each of `ExceptionScoping.fss` and `oddJuxt.fss` now carries — neither names anything else the compile path lacks, though neither was measured reaching a run, so "clear" means clear of errors and not shown to pass — and would spare the later library route the renames in `List.fss`, `Set.fss`, `Map.fss` and `PureList.fss`. Its cost is that `= Nothing`, the only spelling of a `Maybe` value the prose chapters ever write, would be a static error in the compiler world for good, and this world would carry the interpreter's acknowledged workaround for a feature it does not need the workaround for. The library route is a reserved fork and those files will be rewritten line by line when it opens; `convenience.tex` will not be rewritten. Two ladder files whose spelling the specification does not sanction were judged the smaller loss, and they are not lost silently: they become ledger row 331 in `record.md`, which names the spelling, both probes, and where the fix lies.

**A second decision: beside `Option`, not over it.** `Maybe` is a second copy of the `Condition` protocol rather than built on `Option`. Three ways to build it over `Option` were considered and rejected. Making `Maybe[\T\]` extend `Option[\T\]` fails because `Option` is declared `comprises { NoneObject[\E19\], Some[\E19\] }` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:650`) and a `comprises` clause is closed, so it would have to be widened — a change to a declared type the prelude already has, which `CLIMB-BATCH-1.md` reserves as a stop. Making `Just`/`NothingObject` wrap a `Some`/`NoneObject` field would put an indirection and an allocation under every method to save one-line bodies. A type alias is not available: `Specification/fortress/preamble.tex:81` lists type aliases among the features not yet supported. The copy costs 56 lines of one-line bodies in `CompilerLibrary.fss`; that was judged cheaper than any of the three, and it is also what the team's draft does — its `Maybe` extends `Condition[\T\]`, not `Option`.

**A third, smaller: the commented draft was replaced, not left beside the live code.** `CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229` now holds live declarations in place of the comment. Leaving the comment beside working declarations of the same names would be a stale second answer in the source, and `explorations/protocol.md` keeps rationale out of the tree. The draft is quoted in full in §4 of this report and recoverable at `git show cb242a2d8:Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi`, so nothing is lost.

## 6. What changed

`Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-234` — the commented draft replaced by live declarations: `value trait Maybe[\T extends Any\] extends { Condition[\T\] } comprises { Just[\T\], NothingObject[\T\] }` with `coerce(_: Nothing)`, `getter isNothing(): Boolean`, `seq(): Maybe[\T\]`, `abstract filter(f: T -> Condition[\()\]): Maybe[\T\]` and a commented `opr SQCAP`; `value object Just[\T extends Any\](x: T)`; `value object NothingObject[\T extends Any\]`; `value object Nothing end`. Member for member the api's `Option` block (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649-661`), plus `isNothing`.

`Library/CompilerLibrary.fss:522-580` — the bodies, inserted before the "Making vectors" section so the component's order matches the api's. Member for member the bodies of `Option`, `Some`, `NoneObject` and the value object `None` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:1308-1367`; `value object None end` is `:1367`, which is where the block ends) with `Option`→`Maybe`, `Some`→`Just`, `NoneObject`→`NothingObject`, `None`→`Nothing`, the static parameter names `E19`/`E20`/`E21` collapsed to `T`, plus `getter isNothing(): Boolean = NOT self.holds` in the trait.

`ProjectFortress/library_tests/MaybeRungM.fss`, `MaybeRungM.test` — the test. It constructs both cases through a function of a run-time `Boolean` so a body returning a constant would not pass; writes the empty case a second time as `coerced: Maybe[\ZZ32\] = Nothing`; and checks `holds`, `isNothing`, `size`, `get`, `getDefault` with and without a default, `NotFound` thrown by `get` on the empty case, `cond`, `typecase`, a `for` over all three values, `reduce`, and `asString`. The `.test` file is `tests=MaybeRungM` / `link` / `run` / `run_out_contains=PASS` / `run_out_does_not_contain=FAIL` — the two checks `FileTests.java:147` and `:155` implement and 22 `.test` files already use, and the form R1 of the repair batch settled on. Not `run_out_WIcontains`, which `library_tests/Boolean.test` and `PLAN.md` write and which the harness has no case for: `generalTestFailed` implements `_contains`, `_does_not_contain`, `_matches`, `_WImatches`, `_WCIequals` and `_equals` (`FileTests.java:147,155,163,171,180,190`) and nothing else.

## 7. Deviations

1. The specification's single `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] ... where {T extends Object}` (`convenience.tex:49`) becomes `value object NothingObject[\T\] extends Maybe[\T\]` plus `value object Nothing end` plus `coerce(_: Nothing) = NothingObject[\T\]`, because that declaration compiles on neither path (`probes/WhereClauseNothing.txt`) and `CodeGen.java:4088` refuses a where clause on an object in any case. The semantics are preserved at all three positions the specification uses the value in (`probes/MaybeCoercionSites.txt`); the spelling `Nothing[\T\]` is not preserved (the ledger row).
2. The specification writes `object`, this writes `value object`, for `Maybe`, `Just`, `NothingObject` and `Nothing` alike — following `Option` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649-661`), the interpreter (`FortressLibrary.fss:1306-1342`) and the draft (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229`), all three of which make the type a value type. The test passes both literal kinds for this reason.

`ProjectFortress/library_tests/TimingRungT.fss` and `.test`, in the format of `library_tests/Boolean.test`: `tests=`, `link`, `run`, and `run_out_contains=PASS` — not `run_out_WIcontains`, which `Boolean.test` and `PLAN.md` write and which the harness does not implement (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:147` checks `_contains`; an unknown key falls through to the default at `:266-270`).

# The gap ledger: how its rows were written and read, and a form for them

Reader: the curator. This note proposes and changes nothing. Section 4 holds the proposal and the decisions it leaves to the curator.

## 0. Scope, terms and method

Scope.

- Read-only. Main was at `a6b594799` when I started. The ledger last changed in `0cf66dbdb` (2026-10-03), so every number below is for that text.
- The ledger is `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md`: 1,250,447 bytes, 1,219 lines.

Terms.

- **Row**: a table line that starts `| N |` above the heading `## Revival worklist`. There are 638.
- **Cell**: one of the eight columns `# | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround`.
- **Closed row**: a row whose defect was fixed. Section 2.7 shows five ways the ledger marks one.
- **Restatement** (this note's word for a duplicate): a later row that records the same defect at the same site as an earlier row, so that its claim could be one sentence of the earlier row.
- **Sibling**: a row with the same mechanism as another row at a different site, operation or path. It needs its own reproducer and fix.
- **Era**: a span of dates in which rows were entered the same way (the table in 1.1).
- **Length**: characters of the whole table line, counted by script. `awk` `length` counts bytes and gives totals 0.3% higher.
- **Climb batch**: one run of the batch workflow script (`explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js`). It starts rung workers in parallel worktrees. **Rung**: one unit of a batch's work. **Skeptic**: an agent that checks a rung worker's work. **Judge**: an agent that rules between a worker and a skeptic. **Gather**: the stage that folds every rung's `record.md` (its finished lines for FACTS, the ledger and the handover) into the record files. **Merged-diff review**: the last review of a folded batch.
- **Run**: one of the microGPT ports of era A (`run-b`, `run-b2`, `run-c`, ...), each with its own `gaps.md`.
- **Home**: where a defect that a rung measures and does not repair is recorded (`climb-batch-workflow.js:1014-1018`). Home 1: repaired, with a passing assertion in the rung's test. ## FACTS.md

- **A top-level variable imported through an api can be read, assigned and read back on the compiled path (2026-09-20, rung X of climb batch 2).** Mutability was lost twice on the way across the api boundary and both sites are repaired: the checker asked the *component's* type environment whether an api-qualified name was mutable and so refused every such assignment with "Cannot assign to immutable variable" (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Operators.scala:444`, now routed through the new `isMutableName`, `scala_src/typechecker/STypeChecker.scala:345-350`, written after its four api-aware siblings at `:307,324,334,356`); and `CodeGen.forVarRef`'s fresh-import path built a plain `VarCodeGen.StaticBinding` with the value's descriptor while a mutable variable's singleton field holds R1's `MutableFValue` cell, so the run died with `NoSuchFieldError` (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5985-5998`, mutability now read from the declaring api's index by `importedVarIsMutable:5960-5967`, the branch `addTopLevelVarBinding:5945-5951` already made for a component's own variables). Gated by `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/ExportVarRungX.test` with `ExportVarRungXApi.fsi`/`.fss` beside it. `NamingCzar.java` is not touched.
- **An exported function fails exactly as an exported variable does when a component's name differs from the api it exports, and the failure is the repository's, not codegen's (2026-09-20, rung X).** `probes/FnApi.fsi`+`FnLib.fss`+`FnMain.fss` dies with `NoClassDefFoundError: FnApi`, alongside `P8Api$shared` and `P9Api$shared` (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-export-var/probes/probes-preedit.txt:29,96,163`). Through the real entry points the divergence never reaches codegen at all: `fortress link P8Main` and `walk` on each of the three main components print "Could not find an implementation for API ... on path" (`probes/link-and-walk-preedit.txt:4-9,45-60`), so both execution paths assume the api and its implementing component share a name. The assumption is `Linker.whoIsImplementingMyAPI`'s fallback to the api's own name (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/linker/Linker.java:72-76`) when nothing has been registered in its persisted map, and only the user can register one, by hand, through `LinkShell`'s `alink`/`clink` verbs (`linker/LinkShell.java:41-70`; `linker/README:28-40` describes the intended design). `Specification/basic/components/overview.tex:33-35` settles it -- a reference to an imported api is "resolved to a component that exports that api" -- and the team reserved the codegen half of the repair in three comments in one file (`CodeGen.java:411-441`, `:1856`, `:6599-6606`). Gated as an expected failure by `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXExportVarRungXLinked.test`.
- **An immutable top-level variable exported through a same-named api already worked before rung X, including at an object type (2026-09-20, rung X).** `probes/SameVarApi.*` prints `fixed = 11` and `probes/ObjVarApi.*`+`ObjVarMain.fss` prints `data.size = 5` with exit 0 on the base tree (`probes/probes-preedit.txt:218`, `probes/link-and-walk-preedit.txt:42-44`). Both microGPT apis export `corpus: Corpus` immutably from an api that shares its component's name (`explorations/apl/mg/MicroGptApl.fsi:18` declares it, `MicroGptApl.fss:12-13` is `component MicroGptApl` exporting `MicroGptApl`; `explorations/run-c4/src/MicroGptFlat.fsi:16` declares it, `MicroGptFlat.fss:9-10` is `component MicroGptFlat` exporting `MicroGptFlat`, and the satisfying declaration is the immutable `corpus: Corpus = loadCorpus(corpusPath, blockSize, bosId)` at `MicroGptFlat.fss:48`), and `MicroGptFlatCheck.fss:38,40,72` is the second component that reads it -- so the shape the two target programs actually use was never blocked, and what rung X adds for them is the mutable case.
- **`ant compileAll` deletes a tracked file (2026-09-20, rung X).** `compileAll` depends on `compileCommon` (`build.xml:539`), which depends on `cleanCache` (`:715`), which deletes `default_repository/caches` entire (`:42,356-359`) -- including the tracked `global.map`, the linker's persisted `RepoState` (`linker/RepoState.java:176`). Every worktree that runs `ant compileAll` therefore shows `D default_repository/caches/global.map` afterwards, and a `git add -A` at that moment commits the deletion; restore it with `git checkout -- default_repository/caches/global.map`.
- **An `XXX*.test` file in `compiler_tests/` cannot carry a `run_out_contains` key (2026-09-20, rung X).** `FileTests.java:583-585` tests `trueFailure != null` before `:587`'s `shouldFail != failed`, so the unmet output assertion fails the test whatever the XXX name says (corrected here by the merged-diff review of 2026-09-20; the version folded into FACTS.md at the gather stage already carries the two line numbers, this staging copy did not); this is one face of the harness author's own warning at `FileTests.java:853`. All 224 existing `XXX*.test` files in that directory assert a diagnostic from a `compile`-family command and none has a `run` line, which is a constraint and not a habit. `XXX0b.test` is the model: it asserts the same "Could not find an implementation for API" diagnostic for a different api.

## Gap ledger

**Row 320** -- append to the notes, do not renumber:

> Repaired in part by rung X of climb batch 2 (2026-09-20), which split the row into two defects and measured that only one of them is the variable's. **Repaired:** mutability is no longer lost when the declaration crosses the api boundary, at both of the two sites that dropped it -- the checker's `env.isMutable(id)` on the importing component's environment (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Operators.scala:444`, which refused every assignment to an imported mutable variable with "Cannot assign to immutable variable" *before* codegen was ever reached, a third failure mode the row did not name) and `CodeGen.forVarRef`'s always-`StaticBinding` fresh-import path (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5985-5998`). One further correction to the row's premise: the shape both microGPT apis use -- an *immutable* variable exported from an api that shares its component's name -- already worked before this rung, at `ZZ32` and at an object type (`probes/probes-preedit.txt:218`, `probes/link-and-walk-preedit.txt:42-44`).

**Rows 343 and 344, both rewritten at the gather stage on the skeptic's required
correction 1.** The row this rung first wrote — "the interpreter cannot see a mutable
top-level variable exported through an api at all", NEGATIVE-VERIFIED — was refuted by
`probes/skeptic/skeptic-name-isolation.txt` and is **not** opened. It generalised from one
probe whose variable happened to be called `shared`. What went into the ledger instead, in
manifest order from 343, is the skeptic's pair: 343, the unreported name collision, and
344, the compiler prelude's missing locality functions. Both are folded in full in
`explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md` (section 10's table) and neither needs restating
here; the two differences from the skeptic's proposed text are that the assignment claim
is now measured (`probes/gather/GatherAssignApi.fsi`+`.fss`+`GatherAssignMain.fss`,
capture `probes/gather/gather-assign.txt`: read 7, assign 23, read back 23, at one thread
and at four), and that row 343's notes correct this rung's report on where its gated home
is: `ProjectFortress/tests/` does honour an `XXX` name — `FileTests.java:711` hands
`s.startsWith("XXX")` to `SourceFileTest` as `shouldFail` and `:384-404` turns such a file
red the day it starts passing, 55 `XXX*.fss` already live there, and
`tests/XXXImportImportCollision.fss` is that corpus's own collision test, importing its
api pair from `ProjectFortress/test_library/`. The reason rung X did not add it is only
that this batch forbids running `ant testSystem`, so it could not be verified before
landing.

**Row 13** (import aliasing) — appended, not renumbered: the skeptic's two-path
measurement of `import SkVarApi.{counter => ctr}`, refused identically by both paths three
times each with "Variable ctr is not defined." (`probes/skeptic/SkAlias.fss`, capture
`probes/skeptic/skeptic-differentials.txt:20-28`, `:104-111`, `:135-143`, `:219-226`).

and its claim ("binds nothing") had no compiled-path witness.

## Handover state line

Climb batch 2, rung X (`rung-export-var`) landed as one commit composed at the gather stage, of which that branch is not a parent: a mutable top-level variable imported through an api can now be read, assigned and read back on the compiled path, repaired at the two places mutability was dropped -- one in the type checker, one in codegen -- with `compiler_tests/ExportVarRungX.test` gating it at one thread and at four and `compiler_tests/XXXExportVarRungXFrozen.test`, added at the gather stage, gating the refusal the widened check must not lose. - **`round` on a float sends an exact half to the even integer on both paths as of rung R of climb batch 3** (2026-09-22, `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/REPORT.md`). The interpreter's two float natives, `Float$Round` and `RR32$Round`, are now `(long) Math.rint(…)` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/Float.java:384`, `RR32.java:326`), the call the compiled path's `simpleDoubleArith.doubleRound` has made since rung F (`nativeHelpers/simpleDoubleArith.java:132-134`). A float literal reaches `Float$Round` through `trait Number`'s `round` body (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:422`), so those two natives are every float `round` in `walk`. `walk` now answers `round(2.5) = 2`, `round(-3.5) = -4`, `round(0.5) = 0` and `round(-1.5) = -2` on `RR64`, and the same plus `round(4.5) = 4` on `RR32`, gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/RoundHalfEvenRungR.fss` (21 assertions). Its compiled twin prints the same eleven `RR64` lines as `walk` (`compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/RoundHalfEvenCompiledProbe.txt` against `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/RoundHalfEvenWalkProbe-after.txt`). ## Ledger rows proposed, not added

**Proposal A (highest).** *A top-level mutable variable compiled by the code generator is not transactional and not volatile.* Kind: implementation gap, NEGATIVE, unverified by execution. Spec: `Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex:37-42` and `:65-67`; `Specification/basic/memory-model.tex:34-42`, `:69-76`. Evidence: `VarCodeGen.MutableStaticBinding` at `VarCodeGen.java:302-325` against `LocalMutableVar` at `:371-473` and `MutableTaskVarCodeGen` at `:529-655`; `MutableFValue.java:18` (`volatile`); `CodeGen.forAtomicBlock` at `CodeGen.java:1729-1757`; interpreter comparison `BaseEnv.java:599-601`, `ReferenceCell.java:24-26,123-188`. Notes: row 312's neighbour and its consequence; the repair is to hold the singleton field's value in a `MutableFValue` and reuse `LocalMutableVar`'s branch; `MutableFieldVar` (`VarCodeGen.java:197-230`) has the same hole for object fields and predates th

**Proposal B.** *`Condition[\E18\]`'s `excludes` clause is commented out, so `Boolean` excludes neither `String` nor the numeric types in the compiler world.* Kind: dormant code with a live consequence. Evidence: `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:622`, `.fss:1281`; the Meet Rule at `Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:247-262`; the pair `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:36` and `:47` that now depends on it. Notes: restoring the clause would discharge the obligation rather than create one; whether the `OverloadingChecker` is incomplete for this pair is the open question, and answering it is one `fortress compile` of a two-declaration probe.

**Proposal C.** *`HasRank`'s `opr =` and its `AnyMaybe` exclusion must be restored when the compiler world gains array traits and `Maybe`.* Kind: deliberate omission carrying a debt. Evidence: `Library/CompilerLibrary.fss:555-557` against `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1584-1589` and the override at `:1861-1866`; `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:813` for `AnyMaybe`; `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649-659` for the compiler world's `Option`. Notes: nothing observes it today; the array rung is where it comes due, and rows 71 and 288 are where the note belongs if no new row is wanted.

## Scope of the repair, and the one fork already reserved

The scope question Proposal A raises is not a new fork and is not sent up: `POSITIONS.md` (2026-09-17) records that an undecided point is a reason for a deeper pass, not a halt, and that only forks already reserved in `PLAN.md` reach Pavol.

The deeper pass here is one question answered once, for the compiled path's mutable state as a whole rather than for top-level variables alone: `VarCodeGen.MutableFieldVar` (`VarCodeGen.java:197-230`) writes an object's mutable field with a bare `PUTFIELD` and has the same hole, it predates the revival, and `Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex:37-42` does not distinguish a variable from a field. Repairing only top-level variables leaves the language observably half transactional, so the repair should be designed across `MutableStaticBinding` and `MutableFieldVar` together and landed in whatever order the tests allow.

The one fork here that `PLAN.md` does reserve is the library route — whether the compiler world's algebraic and generator layer is grown from `Library/CompilerAlgebra` and `Library/GeneratorLibrary`, which rung 1 has now made reachable, or kept monomorphic. `map/dormant-code.md:107-114` frames it, `PLAN.md`'s stop conditions name it, and rungs 2, 3 and 5 each refused it by name.

## Not verified

Nothing was built or run for this review, by instruction; every behavioural claim about the landed code is read off the bytecode the generators emit and the spec text, not off an execution.

Whether `Boolean` and `String` in fact exclude in the compiler world's `TypeAnalyzer` was not determined; the reading above says they do not, the `OverloadingChecker`'s silence says they might, and a two-declaration probe settles it.

Whether a body typed `Any` reaches the monomorphic `===` overloads on the compiled path was not determined; a component declaring `chk(a: Any, b: Any): Boolean = (a === b)` and calling it on two separately computed `RR64` values settles it in one compile and one run.

Whether any lifted (coercion) static argument's bound was only checkable through the walk rung 1 removed was not determined.

The ladder's own numbers (pass counts 59 → 67 → 75, the subset tables) were taken from the rungs' reports and were not re-measured.

## Proposed ledger changes, for the coordinator to make or reject

I have added nothing. These are proposals.

**Amend row 317**, four additions: that `ZZ.coerce(x: IntLiteral) = x.asZZ` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:501`) puts `-1` into the type the spec defines as all finite integers, which is the row's strongest single statement and is currently absent; that `ZZ32.coerce` defeats `FIntLiteral.asZZ32`'s own range check rather than merely returning a wrong value; that the repair is `l <= 31` and `l <= 63` at `CodeGen.java:3864,3874` **coupled** to `FIntLiteral.asNN32`/`asNN64` learning to read `largerVal`, because those two currently depend on the wrap; and that the `ZZ64.coerce` citation is now `:562`.

**Amend row 317's spec column** to add `basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:369-370,400-401`, which is what makes this a violation rather than an unaddressed case: wrapping in Fortress has its own operator spellings, so silent wrapping is not an implementation liberty.

**Open a new row** for the folded-against-run-time disagreement: the same literal arithmetic answers `4294967296` when written as two literals and `0` when written through two variables, `IntegerLiteralFoldingVisitor.java:162-168` against `compile-ladder/rung7/probes/p39.*`. Status should be UNVERIFIED until someone runs the two-line probe; I did not run it.

**Open a new row** for rung 7's semantics divergence: `a = 2147483647; b = 2; println (a b)` gives `4294967294` compiled and `-2` under `walk`, created by `2027f519b`, with the three candidate answers named — exact numeral arithmetic (what landed, and what the team's folder does), coercion to `ZZ32` then `IntegerOverflow` (what the compiler world's own checked arithmetic implies), and the interpreter's silent wrap (which `basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:369-370` says should not exist). This row is a fork, not a bug.

**Open a small row** for the dark `compiler_tests/IntegerLiteralsFolding.fss`: the team's own test of a phase that is wired into `compilerPhaseOrder` and has never been run in this lineage.

**Amend row 316** with one sentence: the separator is LF where the interpreter's is `lineSeparator`, so the two backends' output differs on any platform whose separator is not LF.

---

## Decisions the deeper pass owes, and the one fork that reaches Pavol

POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-17: new forks invented at the point of difficulty do not reach Pavol; the forks already reserved in `PLAN.md` do. So these are sorted by that rule rather than presented as four equal questions.

**Reaches Pavol, because it is reserved.** Not the wrap — the spec settles that one and it is a scheduled rung, not a fork. The fork is what type an untyped literal's arithmetic happens at. `PLAN.md:47` reserves "any change of semantics against the spec", and rung 7 made the operation happen at the numeral type where `literals.tex:132-148` puts it after coercion at a number type; the spec is silent only on *which* number type. That silence is what makes the rest of it a decision rather than a defect: the compiler world folds literal arithmetic exactly before typecheck (`PhaseOrder.java:142`) and throws `IntegerOverflow` on `ZZ32` (`simpleIntArith.java:94-98`), where the interpreter computes at the narrowest applicable type and wraps silently, which `basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:369-370` says should not happen at all. The ladder's success criterion is "output byte-identical to `walk`", and on integer literals the interpreter cannot be both the oracle and wrong. Either the interpreter stops being the oracle for this one area, or the compiler world's folding and checking are what change. The rungs took the first answer without saying so, which is why this is the item on the list tha

**For the deeper pass, not for Pavol: where literal arithmetic lives.** The team put it in a compile-time phase and left the run-time bodies throwing; rung 7 put it at run time and left the phase alone. Both now exist over overlapping families and disagree with each other on the same values. Keep both and make them agree, retire the phase in favour of the bodies, or widen the phase and return the bodies to throwing — an architecture call the next rung should make and execute, with a test that pins both spellings of the same expression.
